title: Probabilistic Topic Modeling With Transformer Representations
venue: IEEE Transactions on Neural Networks and Learning Systems
subcategory: VAE-based probabilistic model with topics as Gaussians in transformer embedding space
task: Topic discovery with calibrated document-topic and word-topic probabilities
problem: Clustering-based models (BERTopic, Top2Vec) assign topics heuristically, while LDA-style models ignore transformer embedding spaces.
architecture: TNTM: LDA-like generative process in which each topic is a multivariate normal distribution in a transformer word-embedding space (dimension reduced with UMAP); inference with a VAE whose encoder can take sentence embeddings; GMM clustering initialises topics for faster, more stable inference.
llm_or_encoder: Transformer word embeddings; document embeddings from all-MiniLM-L6-v2; evaluation embeddings from paraphrase-MiniLM-L6-v2
key_results: 20 Newsgroups, 20 topics: embedding coherence 0.370 (TNTM with document embeddings) vs 0.341 for Top2Vec, the best baseline; topic diversity 1.00.
Topic diversity stays close to 1 even with 200 topics, whereas other models degrade as the number of topics grows.
strengths: Fully probabilistic document-topic assignments instead of heuristic cluster labels.
Topics defined relative to an embedding model allow out-of-vocabulary enrichment and new-document inference.
Hyper-parameters of all baselines tuned with Bayesian optimisation (OCTIS).

limitations.text: NPMI of TNTM (-0.071 and -0.083 on 20 Newsgroups, 20 topics) is lower than Top2Vec (0.164) and BERTopic (0.033); the authors argue PMI-based coherence is unreliable for neural models and use embedding coherence instead.
Future work is needed for short and sparse texts.

notes: Numbers are from the arXiv version; the published TNNLS version may differ slightly.
